prompt:
I need the front end for Capstone Commons. A shared workspace a university's nonprofit management program uses for capstone projects, where student teams build real deliverables for community partner organizations with their instructor and partner contacts involved.

Who's using it: Jordan Kim, a senior on a four-student team in the Nonprofit Financial Management capstone. Jordan is responsible for the expense side of the budget the team is building for Second Chance Paws, a small animal rescue. The class is on Jordan's laptop in the library, and Jordan is fairly good with spreadsheets.

What they're doing right now: The FY2027 operating budget draft is due to the rescue's executive director on Friday. Opening it tonight, Jordan sees the veterinary care line has jumped from $48,000 to $71,500 since yesterday. Jordan needs to know who changed it and when, and whether it was a teammate or the rescue's director, Pam, who can comment but supposedly not edit. It also matters what reason was given, because the change wipes out the surplus in the conservative revenue scenario. Two teammates are online right now. Jordan wants to talk it through with them, settle on the vet figure, possibly put back the earlier value, and flag the change for Professor Adeyemi, who grades each student's individual contributions.

What's in the system at this point: Budget for Second Chance Paws (annual budget around $310,000): 64 line items in 9 categories, 3 revenue scenarios (conservative $286,000, expected $318,000, optimistic $352,000), and assumption notes for each line. Team: Jordan Kim, Aaliyah Brooks, Mateo Ruiz, Sun-hee Park (editors). Pam Whitfield, executive director, can comment only. Prof. Kemi Adeyemi can do everything, including grading. Change history: 412 edits since 2 Nov 2026, each with author, time, old and new values. The vet care line was changed by Mateo at 11:42pm on 19 Nov with the note 'per Pam's email — new clinic rates', after Pam commented 'Our vet is raising rates 40% in Feb.' 17 open comments. Milestones: draft due 27 Nov, final 11 Dec.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
